title: Article 15 Referral Package
thesis: Communication to the Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court under Rome Statute Article 15. Crimes against humanity (Rome Statute Article 7) committed by the Government of Canada through the Track 2 Medical Assistance in Dying program. Filed pursuant to the public-information mechanism the Statute creates for any person.

scenes.headline: Article 15 Referral Package
scenes.subhead: Communication to the Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court — Rome Statute Article 7 (crimes against humanity).

scenes.headline: Cover — to the Office of the Prosecutor
scenes.body:
To: Office of the Prosecutor, International Criminal Court
Attention: Karim A. A. Khan KC, Prosecutor
Re: Article 15 communication regarding crimes against humanity committed by the Government of Canada — Track 2 Medical Assistance in Dying
Filed by: TENET5 accountability project, on behalf of the Canadian public record

This package is submitted under Article 15 of the Rome Statute, which permits any person to submit information on crimes within the jurisdiction of the Court. The submission supplements and corroborates the existing Article 15 communication filed by Roger Foley, OTP-CR-XXXX/23, February 2023.

The information herein establishes a prima facie case that crimes against humanity under Article 7(1)(a), 7(1)(b), 7(1)(h), and 7(1)(k) have been committed in Canada from 2021 through 2024 inclusive, and that those crimes are ongoing.

scenes.headline: Statement of facts (summary)
scenes.body:
1. The Government of Canada enacted Bill C-7 in March 2021, removing the “reasonably foreseeable death” safeguard from the Medical Assistance in Dying (MAID) statute and creating a separate eligibility track (“Track 2”) for persons whose death is NOT foreseeable.
  2. Track 2 has been used to administer state-funded death to disabled, chronically ill, and economically vulnerable Canadians whose underlying suffering is socioeconomic in origin, including persons whose primary precipitating factors were poverty, housing insecurity, and isolation.
  3. By end-2024, Canada had recorded 76,000+ cumulative MAID deaths since 2016, with 16,499 in 2024 alone (5.1% of all Canadian deaths). Track 2 represents 4.7% of MAID deaths and is growing year-over-year.
  4. Ontario’s statutory MAiD Death Review Committee has documented 428+ non-compliance findings and confirmed in its 2024 Vulnerability Report that Track 2 recipients are massively over-represented in the lowest material-resources quintile (28.4% vs 20% population baseline) and the highest residential-instability quintile (48.3%).
  5. Veterans Affairs Canada offered MAID to a wounded combat veteran seeking PTSD treatment. The federal Minister of Veterans Affairs confirmed at least four such incidents in House of Commons committee testimony, 2022-12-01.
  6. The Government of Canada was warned, in writing, before passage of Bill C-7 by Canadian disability-rights organizations, by UN Special Rapporteurs (joint communication January 2021), and after passage by the Ontario Chief Coroner’s reports and by the existing Article 15 communication of Roger Foley. None of these warnings has resulted in restriction of Track 2.

scenes.headline: Crimes alleged — Rome Statute Article 7
scenes.body:
Chapeau (Article 7(1)): widespread or systematic attack directed against any civilian population (the disabled, chronically ill, and economically vulnerable Canadians eligible under Track 2), with knowledge of the attack (state knowledge documented on the parliamentary record, in federal Health Canada annual reports, and via the Foley Article 15 communication).

  • 7(1)(a) Murder — Track 2 provisions documented by the Ontario Chief Coroner where the suffering driving the request was rooted in unmet social needs and reasonable treatment alternatives were not adequately explored.
  • 7(1)(b) Extermination — per the 7(2)(b) definition, the intentional infliction of conditions of life calculated to bring about the destruction of part of a population. Federal denial of housing, income, and palliative care to the same population offered MAID. Ontario MDRC quintile data documents the population-level pattern.
  • 7(1)(h) Persecution on disability grounds — disability is a recognized “other ground” under Article 7(1)(h) by reference to the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (Canada ratified 2010). Roger Foley’s case is the documented test.
  • 7(1)(k) Other inhumane acts — the Wardoll labelling operation conducted from inside the Canadian Forces, branding Canadians who oppose Track 2 as ideologically motivated violent extremists. Documented in the TENET5 foreign-influence pipeline.

scenes.headline: Submission
scenes.body:
This Article 15 communication is filed pursuant to Rome Statute Article 15(1) and (2), which provide that the Prosecutor may receive information on crimes within the jurisdiction of the Court from any source. The Prosecutor is requested to:

  1. Open a preliminary examination into the conduct described above pursuant to Article 15(3).
  2. Consolidate this submission with the existing Article 15 communication of Roger Foley (OTP-CR-XXXX/23) and any other communications received concerning Canadian Track 2 MAID conduct.
  3. Notify the submitter of any decision pursuant to Article 15(6) and Regulation 49 of the Regulations of the Court.

Submitted by: Daniel Perry, Canadian Forces combat veteran (Afghanistan), maintainer of the TENET5 accountability dossier at https://tenet-5.github.io.
